entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: So many cases of extortion in Shibuya...[n]And now they're saying the mafia's[n]behind them.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Wasn't your office in Shibuya?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Oh, yeah. But I'd already left... Though[n]I'm sure I would have been a target of[n]harassment myself.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Have you ever seen the mafia?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: I don't remember. I only walked along[n]the major streets between the station[n]and the office.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Or it could be I just wasn't paying[n]attention to anything but work.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: You know, the Phantom Thieves are[n]okay by me.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: It might just be a whim of youth, but[n]there are times when naïve justice is[n]called for.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: At first I thought it was a bunch of kids[n]pulling pranks, but now I'm impressed.[n]I wonder what they're going to do next.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: In fact... I wish they'd bring a change[n]of heart to someone I know.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Even you think of stuff like that?[n]Mind if I ask whose heart?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Huh? Oh... It's my wife.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: She's scary! The woman's a fiend,[n]I tell ya! Haha!

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: They say Japan's economy is in trouble[n]thanks to Medjed. I wonder if it's going[n]to be like when the bubble burst...

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: The company I was working at survived,[n]but it was a slaughterhouse elsewhere...

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: The bubble, huh... Brings back memories.[n]That's about the time I left home.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: If it weren't for the former owner, I might[n]have been a monk right about now.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Whoa! First time I'm hearing that one.[n]Were you training to become a monk?

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: My home was a Buddhist temple. And[n]my older brothers had no intention of[n]taking over the business.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: It turns out, neither did I! I wanted to be[n]free, and this is where I ended up. Still[n]doing whatever I want.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: It seems like wherever you go, everyone's[n]talking about the Phantom Thieves. Are[n]your kids into them, too?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: No, I'm the only one rooting for them![n]My son's studying for entrance exams...

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Studying's good, right? Some of my[n]customers are students and they're[n]brilliant.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Yeah, sure. But academics isn't the[n]only path. You can have more freedom[n]in life...

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: I think about the other possibilities often,[n]maybe because I myself was loyal to the[n]company I worked for before.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: If Okumura is a criminal, then his heart[n]should be changed. Those big companies[n]have too many rotten eggs!

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: But if the business doesn't perform well[n]because of that, wouldn't that lead to[n]more restructuring?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: ...Maybe. Still, evil must perish. I bet the[n]Phantom Thieves will take things in the[n]right direction.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: A scalpel may be needed at times, but[n]don't you think it's dangerous to have[n]blind faith in it?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: The Phantom Thieves might be done for[n]now... I was really hoping for them to[n]change the world...

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Well, the situation might be tough for[n]them now, but I hope they find their[n]own solution.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Like free jazz, which was newly born out[n]of structured performances like bebop.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Bebop was ad-libbing, right? It reached[n]limits in its predictability...

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Right. But reaching certain limits doesn't[n]mean it's lost all meaning. One might see[n]and bear new ways of thinking from it...

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: I look forward to seeing what they do[n]next. Don't you?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: There's a reward for catching the[n]Phantom Thieves... Maybe I should[n]try getting 'em.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: What happened? I thought you were[n]supportive of them.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Now that I'm not working, I've got[n]a lot of free time. It's my bebop after[n]retirement.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: This may be unwanted advice, but...

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Even bebop was ad-libbing within certain[n]rules. When your playing goes out of[n]control, you just might destroy the song.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Hijacking the airwaves... Wow.[n]So that's their solution.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: I wonder if the Phantom Thieves will[n]succeed in changing Shido's heart...

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: The backlash against them was fierce...[n]They just might fail this time.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: You seem awfully worried. I thought[n]you were going to capture them for the[n]reward money.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Yeah, I can sure use the money. I can't[n]even afford to pay my kids' tuition[n]at this rate!

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: O-Oh, never mind... Forget I said[n]anything...

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: So, what did you do over the holidays?

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Nothing much happens for a single[n]man like me. But never mind that.[n]What about you?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: We welcomed the new year with[n]the family.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: We haven't done that since... I don't[n]know how long. It felt like a dream...

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Maybe I should venture out and open[n]my own bar, like you.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: ...If it's really what you want to do,[n]you'll have my support.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: But if it isn't, I wouldn't recommend it.[n]All that really matters is what you want[n]to do.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: What I want to do...[n]What do I want to do...?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Looks like this place is doing well.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Maybe you should hire more workers,[n]maybe even part-time.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: I want to, but hiring the right person can[n]be pretty hard.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: ...You want to try working here?[n]You were thinking about opening[n]your own place the other day.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: I come work... for you?[n]Hm, I guess that's a possibility...

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Do what I want to... But what is it that's[n]most important to me...?

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: You seem more relaxed these days.[n]Like a weight's been lifted. Something[n]happen?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: I'm actually contemplating employment[n]again... I told my family everything.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: My kids and my wife were shocked when[n]I told them that I had been restructured.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: I would say that I was going to work, but[n]spend all my time here instead. I even[n]lied to you and told you that I retired.

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: But I finally realized what it is that I[n]want to do... What I have to do...

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Is that so... Well, if you get tired, come[n]and visit me. You're going to need a[n]break once in a while, right?

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Haha! You're right. Besides, joining the[n]work force again isn't going to be easy...

entries.speaker: Stocky Man
entries.en: Well, if I ever feel down, let me blow[n]off some steam and listen to some good[n]old jazz.

...I don't know.
I'm afraid not.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Do me a favor. Next time you see him,[n]tell him to come by again.
But Akechi is already...
There's something in my pocket...
It's Akechi's glove...[n]He promised me a rematch.
...My fight with Akechi isn't over yet.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Well, I won't insist. But you and[n]Akechi-kun can swing by anytime.
Okay.
I'll let him know.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]
entries.en: Yeah. Do come again. I'll be looking[n]forward to it.

entries.speaker: [f 7 2]

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: Yeah! They say they have less stations to[n]reach the further out ones like Tachikawa,[n]but who cares?

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy
entries.en: I bombed the test the other day.[n]They're gonna lower my allowance[n]for sure...

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: Just ace the next one! Wanna go study[n]somewhere?

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy
entries.en: Oh, let's go to the pancake shop near the[n]station! There should be plenty of seats on[n]a weekday.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: I can already tell there's gonna be no[n]studying... Not that I care.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: Kichijoji gets featured on TV a lot, but it's[n]really a lot of chain stores that get crowded[n]on the weekends.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: I've never seen anybody... I guess I[n]wouldn't recognize people like that,[n]though.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy
entries.en: We studied about the origins of Kichijoji[n]today at school, and I learned something[n]new.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl

entries.en: There was. But the temple named Kichijoji[n]was originally in the Suidobashi area.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy
entries.en: But it was burned down in the Great Fire[n]of Meireki. So the people who lived near[n]it moved to this place.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: I guess they were really attached to the[n]name Kichijoji, huh?

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy
entries.en: Ugh. Another special on the internet[n]about Kichijoji being the place to live.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: You know the rankings are just based on[n]the image people have. Actually living[n]here, you'll see it's just full of chain stores.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: Is there another place you want to live?

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy
entries.en: Gotta be Shibuya, of course! Oh, but[n]Ebisu looks like a stylish place, too!

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl
entries.en: Someone's easily influenced by these[n]rankings...

entries.en: The Phantom Thieves scare me. We don't[n]know what they want or anything.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy
entries.en: I heard there's a manga artist who[n]wants to make something based on[n]the Phantom Thieves.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Boy
entries.en: It's going fine, I guess. It's almost been a[n]year since we started dating, so I gotta[n]think of something.

entries.speaker: Kichijoji-Native Girl

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Not even the Phantom Thieves can[n]change your drunken heart.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *hiccup* Ha, that's funny. Wish they'd[n]take my liver instead!

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: I'm gonna post on the Phan-Site[n]one of these days. What would your[n]request be, pops?

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Hmm, let's see... How about something[n]like "I'd like some more affection from[n]my wife"?

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: What a terrible company Okumura[n]Foods is! Don't you agree?

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *hiccup* Y'know, the guy who spread[n]whisky in Japan supposedly said...

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: "When you're done with work, hurry[n]home and spend time with your family."

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Well, I'll be damned. Who knew we had[n]such understanding people in Japan?

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: That's someone we all can learn from.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: On that note, gimme another shot[n]of that whisky, please!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: You know, it doesn't matter how[n]much money you have. It's all over[n]when you die.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *hiccup* Damn right. You don't need[n]a whole lotta money.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: You can hang out in this alley with[n]just 1,000 yen and still have one[n]hell of a good time!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Yessir, this alley is truly a place for[n]cheap drinks and cheap drunks!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: But don't get too drunk now. If you[n]drink any more than that, you'll be[n]the next one to die.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *chuckle* At least I'd die happy![n]Shit, there better be drinks where[n]I'm headed!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: You can get reward money for catching[n]the Phantom Thieves. How about it?

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *chuckle* I'm gonna have to decline.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: I just wanna drink with those guys.[n]Bet I could make a scoop outta that[n]article. *hiccup*

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Sheesh, I can never tell if you're being[n]serious or you're just yanking my chain.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Heh, I'm always serious. Serious at[n]gettin' drunk! *hiccup*

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *hiccup* Hey, listen... My book's[n]comin' out soon.

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Well, it's about time! Seriously, that's[n]good news. This calls for a celebration!

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *chuckle* Thanks. I'm sure gonna[n]enjoy the drinks today.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Although I gotta say, it's a little sad that[n]you're the only one who's willin' to[n]celebrate with me...

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Well, in that case, let's call that[n]guitarist over!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Nothing soothes the soul like a singer[n]and his guitar!

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Man, I love New Year's Day! I can drink[n]all I want and not get shit from anyone!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Still celebrating New Year's? We're[n]already well into the new year!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: If you keep this up, you'll ruin your[n]liver, and your wife and kid won't[n]ever come back.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *chuckle* No need to worry. I've got a[n]liver of steel! My numbers are always[n]normal!

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Ahhh, I'm so happy to be drinking!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Hoo boy... It's only a matter of time[n]before we're attending your funeral.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: That Shido is such an idiot. They don't[n]serve alcohol in prison!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Well, I doubt Shido is a hopeless[n]drunk like you.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *hiccup* But didja know this?

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: There's an urban legend about[n]a way you can make distilled[n]alcohol in your cell...

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Oh god... Is there really nothing but[n]alcohol on your mind?

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: At this rate, you're going to die of[n]alcohol poisoning before the government[n]is overthrown...

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Now listen here! You can only enjoy[n]your drinks while you're alive!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: So don't keep drinking until you end[n]up in the hospital again! Life's good![n]You have a book out now!

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Hahaha, I'm sorry I worried you.[n]When I woke up in the hospital,[n]my wife was bawling her eyes out.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Seeing her face made me come to[n]my senses, so after today, I'm going[n]to lay off the drinks.

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: So this is it, huh? I won't have to deal[n]with your drunk ass ever again?

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Well, good for you. Your book's doing[n]well, and you've got family waiting for[n]you... So go home already!

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: *chuckle* Thanks for being subtle![n]You know, I started the sake report so[n]that I can use it as a guide with my son.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: When he reaches the drinking age,[n]this place is going to be our first stop![n]So don't close the place until then!

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: That old man hasn't come here yet.[n]No wonder I'm drinking in peace.

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: I don't like bad-mouthing my customers,[n]but he makes so much trouble...

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: An old man making trouble...?

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: Hey, do you think they're talking[n]about the elderly man causing[n]trouble in Kichijoji?

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Hey, this ain't no place for a young'un[n]like you. You lookin' for somethin'[n]'round here?
The elderly troublemaker.
The conflict artist.

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Hoo boy... So even kids like you[n]know about him.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: That old man's outta control. He takes[n]drinks from strangers, he starts fights...

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: And when he gets in trouble, he causes[n]a ruckus and tries to mooch money[n]off people.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: What's creepy is the more trouble[n]he makes, the wider his smile gets.
Got a name?
Tell me more.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Oh yeah, the old man's always[n]shoutin' his name over and over.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: Heiji Ono, right?

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Yep, that's the name.

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: All right, we got the name of our target!

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: But you know... I can't be that hard[n]on him. He's around my dad's age.

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: When he complains about his joints[n]hurting on rainy days... I can't help[n]but feel sorry for the old man.

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: I wish he didn't hang around here, but[n]stayed warm with his family instead.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: You might sound awfully sympathetic,[n]but I know you really think he's a[n]pain in the ass.

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: Well, yeah, I'm not denying that...

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: His joints hurt on rainy days? Poor guy.

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: I think we got all the info we need. Why[n]don't we talk about it at the hideout?
Now that you have your target, you need to[n]make sure everyone's on board with the mission.[n]Summon them to the hideout for a vote.

entries.speaker: Sake Reporter
entries.en: That old man hasn't shown up yet.[n]*chuckle* It's so quiet without him.

entries.speaker: Aproned Man
entries.en: I don't like talking bad about old[n]people, but that guy...

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: Ahhh... That's it for finals! Time for[n]summer break!

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: Not that teachers get to relax much.[n]Still got piles of paperwork...

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: But it should be manageable, at least.[n]Maybe my side job can even give me[n]more shifts?

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: Dangit, Dr. Maruki's term's practically[n]over!

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: Should we even do a farewell party?[n]He's definitely earned it...

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: ...But I don't want to be the one to[n]propose it! 'Cause I know I'll get[n]saddled with planning the damn thing!

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: I wish someone like Ms. Chouno would[n]notice. Then she could plan everything...

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: So sorry, Boss! Can I make reservations[n]for tomorrow!?

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: A colleague is leaving tomorrow, and[n]we want to throw a party, but we[n]don't have a venue yet...

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: ...Grah! Why do I have to do this!?

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: I wonder if he's gonna be all right...

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: Well, he's going home. I know there's[n]nothing to worry about...

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: But I can't help it...

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: Ugh... Another week, another fairytale[n]wedding for one of my friends. How[n]many has it been already?

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: Seems like everyone's suddenly so[n]dang happy. What the heck's going on?

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: I mean... it's a little scary. All this joy[n]has to come with a price, right...?

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: ...Maybe I'm overthinking this.

entries.speaker: Ms. Chouno
entries.en: Hmmm... I think we need further[n]investigation inside the school itself.

entries.speaker: Ms. Chouno
entries.en: Even the teachers are on watch.[n]We can't relax just yet!

entries.speaker: Ms. Chouno
entries.en: Summer break isn't just about cautioning[n]our students. It's about understanding[n]where they're coming from!

entries.speaker: Ms. Chouno
entries.en: So many of them see these temptations[n]of summer and just... lose control, you[n]know what I mean?

entries.speaker: Ms. Chouno
entries.en: That's why I have to be a rock for my[n]students! A pillar of stability!

entries.speaker: Ms. Chouno
entries.en: The students seem a bit restless...[n]Maybe it's because they just got back[n]from the school trip.

entries.speaker: Ms. Chouno
entries.en: It's times like these we have to be extra[n]cautious! Starting tomorrow, I'll be[n]watching them like a hawk!

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: Good grief. That news article was the[n]last thing we need. Can't wait for the[n]parent complaints to roll in...

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: *sigh* We have to find an appropriate[n]way to deal with this, and soon. What[n]is the principal thinking?

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: ...He has been looking awfully pale lately.[n]I wonder if something's going on.

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: Why would the principal do this? Why[n]is all of this happening at once?

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: I could tell something was eating at him,[n]but I never expected this...

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: What are we supposed to do now...?

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: December already, huh...? Shujin's made[n]a complete 180 since last year.

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: But I suppose it's not just our school[n]that's changed. Who'd have expected[n]Representative Shido could rise so high?

entries.speaker: Mr. Ushimaru
entries.en: Makes me wonder what next year's[n]going to be like.

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: Hard to believe so many of our students[n]are getting extorted.

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: Maybe it's just that kids today aren't[n]grounded. They don't know how to[n]manage their money seriously...

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: We have to teach them to measure[n]value in more absolute terms instead[n]of basing it on emotion.

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: With the principal gone, the faculty[n]needs to be steadfast in their mission.[n]More than ever.

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: It's just that this ordeal has been so[n]exhausting...

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: ...No. I'm their teacher—I can't let them[n]see me like this.

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: Maybe I should see Dr. Maruki myself.[n]A therapy session might help relieve[n]some of my stress...

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: Oh, that's right. Dr. Maruki's term is[n]almost over.

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: That counseling was originally just to[n]protect the principal's image, but it's[n]done so much for the students...

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: As his colleagues, the least we can do[n]is give him a good sendoff.

entries.speaker: Ms. Usami
entries.en: Ah, well. I'm sure Ms. Kawakami can[n]handle all the logistics herself.

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: We're already in mid-August...

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: The long break came and went without[n]any nasty surprises... Maybe we can[n]finally relax a little.

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: I guess it's possible our first semester[n]was just unusually chaotic...

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: All I can hope for is that we survive our[n]second one.

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: The third-years seem unusually on edge.[n]It's possible it's just exam stress, but...[n]I'm a little concerned.

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: Perhaps Dr. Maruki can help us find[n]a way to deal with this.

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: I should go talk to him...

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: There's something in the air this year.[n]Feels like there's good news everywhere[n]you turn...

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: Most importantly, my wife's been a lot[n]happier. And nothing's better than[n]coming home to see her smile.

entries.speaker: Mr. Inui
entries.en: I wish these days would last forever...

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: I hear some students met with Goro[n]Akechi himself on that field trip.

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: With that razor-sharp intellect, and a[n]dignity beyond his years, he truly is a[n]paragon for them to aspire to.

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: One day, I hope I can partake of that[n]aura... That charisma that won him[n]the moniker of "Detective Prince."

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: So Medjed's declared all-out war.[n]This is getting very interesting.

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: That reminds me of a curious rumor[n]I heard before about Medjed...

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: Apparently, the whole Medjed collective[n]was started by one person alone.

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: It's just a rumor, of course. But if it[n]was true... what kind of peerless[n]genius could have started that?

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: Ahh, the midterms are finally done.[n]What a relief.

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: Well, we teachers still have work to do.

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: All the police visits have left the students[n]uneasy. I hope it doesn't have too much[n]of an impact on their midterm scores...

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: Representative Shido's name has been[n]coming up a lot lately. I suppose he's[n]been making waves in politics...

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: But it's easy for a silver-tongued politician[n]to make promises.

entries.speaker: Mr. Hiruta
entries.en: I suppose we'll just wait and see if he[n]keeps any of them.

entries.speaker: Principal
entries.en: "Are the Phantom Thieves just?" Bah,[n]what does that matter? I just want to[n]know who they are...

entries.speaker: Principal
entries.en: And now, I can't even count on[n]Niijima-kun's cooperation any more...

entries.speaker: Principal
entries.en: I thought once the student extortion case[n]was dealt with, things would finally[n]settle down...

entries.speaker: Principal
entries.en: What's wrong with having a dream!?

entries.speaker: Principal
entries.en: I just want everyone to envy me... I just[n]want to feel like I'm important, and live[n]a life of luxury...

entries.speaker: Principal
entries.en: There is nothing wrong with that, right?[n]That's all I want...

entries.speaker: Principal
entries.en: This is bad... I'm done for...!

entries.speaker: Principal
entries.en: I could turn myself in and tell them[n]everything... No, maybe not... but[n]I have nowhere to run anyway...

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: Woohoo! I got a reliable tipster today,[n]so I think that calls for drinks!

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: Mmmm! It's a nice change of pace to[n]drink somewhere other than Lala-chan's!

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: Hey, barkeep! One more sake and[n]water, please!

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: Aaagh! So many fishy incidents![n]I need a day off...

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: The Phantom Thieves, the psychotic[n]breakdowns... and now Mr. Okumura[n]dies!?

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: I deserve a few tonight! Hey, barkeep![n]Shochu on the rocks, please!

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: He wants to make Japan powerful, huh...?[n]That guy sounds as shady as ever.

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: I bet he's got a few skeletons in his closet.[n]No doubt about it.

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: I don't care if they try to stop me. I'm[n]gonna get to the bottom of this!

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: ...Something doesn't feel right.

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: When you've been a reporter for long[n]enough, you start to see which way the[n]winds are blowing in public opinion.

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: Except now, it feels like the wind's[n]suddenly turned in the complete[n]opposite direction.

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: I mean, everyone's all giddy and happy[n]now... Kinda creeping me out.

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: Hey, you. You know what's going on?

entries.speaker: Ohya
entries.en: ...Of course you don't. Forget I said[n]anything.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: I didn't think working for a big firm[n]would be so boring...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: The execs are all so set in their ways.[n]All their approaches are really behind[n]the times...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Is this really going to be my life now?[n]Years of this, and then I retire?

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: What are the bosses saying? They talk[n]like this mafia stuff has nothing to do[n]with them!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: It wouldn't be happening if they hadn't[n]spent years turning society into a[n]capitalist nightmare!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Both the aggressor and the victim here[n]are looking for easy money. That's the[n]only reason this happens.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: I can't believe our company's so stingy[n]with the IT budget and staff.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: We're a big firm here, guys! Do you[n]realize how much we could lose from[n]a cyberattack?

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: They're not even trying to keep up with[n]the times... How do people like that[n]get promoted?

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: A "Medjed Attack Preparation[n]Committee"? Are they serious?

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Great idea, guys. I love when a bunch of[n]seniority-rule execs with zero IT[n]knowledge tell me how to do my job.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Makes me wish Medjed WOULD take[n]our systems down. Maybe then we'd[n]finally see some goddamn accountability.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: ...What the hell? What did I do? I just[n]wanted to take some time off during[n]the summer.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: All of a sudden, my boss comes at me[n]for being "spoiled" and "lacking drive"?[n]What the hell's his problem?

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: All these old approaches don't work![n]They belong in the past! That's how[n]progress works...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Ugh. I wish Medjed had just taken[n]the whole system down.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Then maybe those stubborn old[n]bureaucrats would finally have[n]gotten the picture.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Inefficient operations, useless "just try[n]harder" philosophy... You can only get[n]so far on "old-school" business practices!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Why are they wasting time on all these[n]inefficient processes?

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Anyone who works overtime is a moron.[n]It just means you failed to measure the[n]man-hours your task needed.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: So what does it say when every person[n]in the company is working overtime?[n]It means something needs to change!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Now everyone's talking about corrupt[n]companies. Welcome to the real world,[n]people.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: There's nothing special about it![n]I mean, look at me! I'm...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: ...I feel like a moron. What AM I[n]working for? Seriously...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Yeah, I'll say it. If you treat your[n]underlings like slaves, you don't deserve[n]to be a boss.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: If we got rid of those people, maybe[n]work would finally be tolerable!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Ugh... I wish I could get rid of my boss,[n]too...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: It's the guys who work overtime who[n]have the problem! How do they not[n]get that!?

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Everyone on the internet agrees with[n]me, so obviously I'm right. My boss is[n]the one who needs to wake up!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: So I leave work on time, and my boss[n]holds that against me? He still doesn't[n]get it!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Dammit... I can't believe I was wrong![n]On paper, I swear that was the most[n]efficient way, but...!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Ugh, and what do they tell me? "Alert us[n]sooner when you're having trouble!"

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: Quit trying to sound like a good boss![n]Like I'd need to lean on you for help!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: I can fix things myself. I don't need[n]some useless exec to interfere...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: It must be nice to have someone like[n]Shido at the top. I wish I had a boss with[n]the skills and understanding he's got...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: If I worked for a guy like him, I could[n]actually believe I'm making a difference.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: He seems like he'd know what's[n]actually efficient. He'd give young[n]people more rewarding work.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: ...I just thought it was my job to be[n]efficient. As a responsible member[n]of society, too.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: As long as I did that, I could do what[n]I wanted, how I wanted. No worrying[n]about what other people think.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: ...I had no idea my boss had been[n]covering for me to the CEO this whole[n]time...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: *sigh*

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: He's been apologizing for me all this[n]time, and I've been treating him like[n]crap.

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: I don't even know how to look him[n]in the eye anymore...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: I never expected to get promoted to[n]assistant manager this fast!

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: All this time, I've been complaining[n]about my boss, but now I'm going[n]to be someone else's boss...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: ...I'd better shape up. Don't want[n]anyone complaining about me...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: My subordinates are talented, and[n]these days, work is fun...

entries.speaker: Young Man in Suit
entries.en: I hope I get assigned to a big project...[n]I'm gonna keep working hard!

entries.speaker: Tired Office Worker
entries.en: If Madarame stole the "Sayuri" from[n]someone else... then who was the[n]original artist?

entries.speaker: Tired Office Worker
